key_insight: Wind-drift-driven Holmboe instability can grow from an infinitesimal disturbance into finite-amplitude, propagating Stokes-like surface waves under background shear.
engineering_relevance: Connecting wave initiation to nonlinear propagation could inform physics-based models of wind-generated ocean waves and air–sea interactions.
method: Analyse linear instability of a uniform air current above a finite-thickness, constant-vorticity water drift layer.
Run two-phase incompressible Navier–Stokes simulations initialised with the fastest-growing eigenmode.
Compare nonlinear wave spectra and profiles with an exact steady travelling-wave boundary-value formulation.
evidence_signal: Simulated exponential growth agrees closely with linear theory, while nonlinear spectra reveal carrier-locked bound harmonics and time-averaged profiles agree well with steady-wave predictions.
watch_item: The findings concern an idealised, gravity-dominated, low-Froude-number configuration before breaking; applicability to turbulent seas and post-breaking dynamics remains unestablished.
paper_title: Oceanic Surface Waves from Wind-Drift-Layer Instability: Exponential Growth to Finite-Amplitude States
